title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

"""Core SVEAD implementation (paper Sections 4.1-4.4, Algorithm 1).

Pipeline per partition k = 1..t:
  R1  sample m anchors uniformly from X without replacement,
  R2  assign every point to its nearest anchor in Euclidean distance
      (implicit Voronoi: no cell boundaries/vertices are built - R11),
  R4  compute per-cell statistics delta_max and delta_mean *before* scoring,
  R3  score s(x) = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean,
  R5  points whose cell contains only the anchor (|Ci| = 1) are skipped
      (NaN) and rely on the remaining partitions,
  R6  final score = arithmetic mean over the partitions that scored the point.

Complexity (R12): O(n*m*d*t).  The n x n Euclidean distance matrix is
precomputed once (O(n^2 d)) so each partition costs O(n*m) memory lookups,
which is exactly the nearest-anchor query of Eq. (1) with a lowest-index
tie-break (numpy argmin).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, Optional, Tuple

import numpy as np


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- geometry
def pairwise_distances(X: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int = 4096) -> np.ndarray:
    """Full Euclidean distance matrix, computed in row chunks."""
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    n = X.shape[0]
    sq = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", X, X)
    D = np.empty((n, n), dtype=np.float64)
    for s in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        e = min(n, s + chunk_rows)
        G = sq[s:e, None] + sq[None, :] - 2.0 * (X[s:e] @ X.T)
        np.maximum(G, 0.0, out=G)
        D[s:e] = np.sqrt(G)
    np.fill_diagonal(D, 0.0)
    return (D + D.T) * 0.5


def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """R1: m distinct row indices drawn uniformly without replacement."""
    m = int(min(max(m, 1), n))
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


# --------------------------------------------------------------- partition
def partition_score(D: np.ndarray, anchors: np.ndarray,
                    out: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
                    out_sum: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
                    out_cnt: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> Dict:
    """One Voronoi partition: assign, cell stats, within-cell score.

    Returns the per-point score vector with NaN for skipped (singleton-cell)
    points plus diagnostics.  If out_sum/out_cnt are given, the score is
    accumulated into them (mean over scored partitions, R6).
    """
    n = D.shape[0]
    m = anchors.size
    sub = D[:, anchors]                       # (n, m) nearest-anchor queries
    cell = np.argmin(sub, axis=1)             # lowest anchor index on ties
    delta = sub[np.arange(n), cell]

    counts = np.bincount(cell, minlength=m).astype(np.float64)
    sum_d = np.bincount(cell, weights=delta, minlength=m)
    max_d = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    np.maximum.at(max_d, cell, delta)         # R4: delta_max per cell

    delta_mean = sum_d / counts               # R4: delta_mean per cell
    dmax_cell = max_d[cell]
    dmean_cell = delta_mean[cell]

    s = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype=np.float64)
    singleton = counts[cell] <= 1             # R5
    good = (~singleton) & (dmax_cell > 0.0)   # degenerate-duplicate guard
    s[good] = (delta[good] / dmax_cell[good]) * dmean_cell[good]
    # points in a multi-point cell whose delta_max == 0 (exact duplicates):
    s[(~singleton) & (dmax_cell <= 0.0)] = 0.0

    if out is not None:
        np.putmask(out, np.isnan(s), 0.0)  # unused path kept explicit
    if out_sum is not None:
        ok = ~singleton
        out_sum[ok] += s[ok]
        out_cnt[ok] += 1.0

    diag = {"n_cells_nonempty": int((counts > 0).sum()),
            "cell_counts": counts,
            "delta_mean": dmean_cell,
            "delta_max": dmax_cell}
    return {"scores": s, "cell": cell, "delta": delta, "diag": diag}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ ensemble
def svead_score(X: np.ndarray, m: int = 128, t: int = 100, seed: int = 1,
                D: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
                agg: str = "mean_scored",
                return_diag: bool = False):
    """SVEAD anomaly scores.  Labels are never consulted (R10).

    agg="mean_scored"  : average over the partitions that scored the point
                         (Section 4.2 "rely on the other t-1 partitions").
    agg="divide_by_t"  : literal Algorithm 1 line 20 (f/t).
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    n = X.shape[0]
    if D is None:
        D = pairwise_distances(X)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    ssum = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    scnt = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    skipped_total = 0
    max_cell = 0
    for k in range(t):
        anchors = sample_anchors(n, m, rng)
        assert np.unique(anchors).size == anchors.size  # R1
        r = partition_score(D, anchors, out_sum=ssum, out_cnt=scnt)
        skipped_total += int(np.isnan(r["scores"]).sum())
        max_cell = max(max_cell, int(r["diag"]["cell_counts"].max()))
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        if agg == "divide_by_t":
            f = ssum / float(t)
        else:
            f = np.where(scnt > 0, ssum / np.maximum(scnt, 1.0), 0.0)
    f[~np.isfinite(f)] = 0.0
    if return_diag:
        return f, {"skipped_fraction": skipped_total / float(n * t),
                   "max_cell_size": max_cell, "m": m, "t": t, "seed": seed,
                   "n": n, "d": X.shape[1], "agg": agg}
    return f

"""Evaluation helpers.  Every function here consumes scores FIRST and labels
second, so labels are only ever touched after predictions exist (R9, R10)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score


def pr_auc_trapezoid(y_true, scores) -> float:
    """Trapezoidal AUC of the precision-recall curve (secondary variant)."""
    from sklearn.metrics import precision_recall_curve

    p, r, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_true, scores)
    return float(np.trapz(p[::-1], r[::-1]))


def evaluate_scores(y_true, scores) -> Dict[str, float]:
    y = np.asarray(y_true).astype(int)
    s = np.asarray(scores, dtype=float)
    return {
        "auc_roc": float(roc_auc_score(y, s)),
        "auc_pr": float(average_precision_score(y, s)),          # ADBench convention
        "auc_pr_trapz": pr_auc_trapezoid(y, s),
    }


def summarize(values: List[float]) -> Dict[str, float]:
    v = np.asarray(list(values), dtype=float)
    return {
        "mean": float(v.mean()),
        "std": float(v.std(ddof=1)) if v.size > 1 else 0.0,
        "std_pop": float(v.std()),
        "min": float(v.min()),
        "max": float(v.max()),
        "n": int(v.size),
    }

"""Variant sensitivity check: aggregation rule and cell-stat scope."""
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from svead.data import load_cardio                                  # noqa: E402
from svead.metrics import evaluate_scores                           # noqa: E402
from svead.svead_core import pairwise_distances, svead_score        # noqa: E402

X, y, prov = load_cardio()
D = pairwise_distances(X)
n = X.shape[0]
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]


def variant(m, t, seed, agg="mean_scored", exclude_anchor=False,
            global_delta_max=False):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    ssum = np.zeros(n)
    scnt = np.zeros(n)
    for k in range(t):
        a = rng.choice(n, m, replace=False)
        sub = D[:, a]
        cell = np.argmin(sub, axis=1)
        delta = sub[np.arange(n), cell]
        counts = np.bincount(cell, minlength=m).astype(float)
        sum_d = np.bincount(cell, weights=delta, minlength=m)
        max_d = np.zeros(m)
        np.maximum.at(max_d, cell, delta)
        if exclude_anchor:
            # cell stats over the non-anchor members only
            is_anchor = np.zeros(n, bool)
            is_anchor[a] = True
            w = (~is_anchor).astype(float)
            cnt2 = np.bincount(cell, weights=w, minlength=m)
            sum2 = np.bincount(cell, weights=delta * w, minlength=m)
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
                dmean = np.where(cnt2 > 0, sum2 / np.maximum(cnt2, 1), 0.0)
            singleton = cnt2[cell] <= 0
        else:
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
                dmean = np.where(counts > 0, sum_d / np.maximum(counts, 1), 0.0)
            singleton = counts[cell] <= 1
        dmax = np.full(m, max_d.max()) if global_delta_max else max_d
        s = np.full(n, np.nan)
        good = (~singleton) & (dmax[cell] > 0)
        s[good] = delta[good] / dmax[cell][good] * dmean[cell][good]
        ok = ~singleton
        ssum[ok] += s[ok]
        scnt[ok] += 1
    f = ssum / t if agg == "divide_by_t" else np.where(scnt > 0, ssum / np.maximum(scnt, 1), 0)
    return f


GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]
for name, kw in [("primary (mean over scored, anchor in stats)", {}),
                 ("divide_by_t (Alg.1 literal)", {"agg": "divide_by_t"}),
                 ("anchor excluded from cell stats", {"exclude_anchor": True}),
                 ("global delta_max", {"global_delta_max": True})]:
    print(f"\n== {name}")
    for m in GRID:
        rs = [evaluate_scores(y, variant(m, 100, s, **kw)) for s in SEEDS]
        a = np.array([r["auc_roc"] for r in rs])
        p = np.array([r["auc_pr"] for r in rs])
        print(f"  m={m:4d} AUC-ROC {a.mean():.4f}+-{a.std(ddof=1):.4f} "
              f"AUC-PR {p.mean():.4f}+-{p.std(ddof=1):.4f}", flush=True)

"""Reproduce C1 (and C2) of "Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly
Detection" (arXiv 2601.03664): SVEAD AUC-ROC / AUC-PR on ADBench `cardio`.

Everything is computed from data by this script - no result number from the
paper is used anywhere in the computation.  The only paper quantities that
appear are the *reported* values kept as comparison metadata for the verdict.

Usage
    python reproduce.py            # full protocol: m-grid x 5 seeds, t=100
    python reproduce.py --force    # ignore selected_config.json cache
    python reproduce.py --seeds 3  # reduced protocol (recorded in notes)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from svead.data import (N_EXPECT, POS_EXPECT, load_cardio)          # noqa: E402
from svead.metrics import evaluate_scores, summarize               # noqa: E402
from svead.svead_core import pairwise_distances, svead_score       # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RESULTS = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")
CONFIG_CACHE = os.path.join(ROOT, "selected_config.json")

M_GRID = [2 ** i for i in range(1, 9)]   # {2^1,...,2^8}  (R7, paper Sec 5.1)
T = 100                                   # ensemble size  (R7, paper Sec 5.1)
SEEDS_DEFAULT = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]          # 5 repeats      (R8, assumption A4)

# Values the paper reports, used ONLY to compute the verdict, never as input.
PAPER_C1_AUC_ROC = 0.9339                 # Table 4, cardio, VEAD column
PAPER_C2_AUC_PR = 0.5356                  # Table 6, cardio, VEAD column
PAPER_C1_STD = 0.0063                     # Table 5 (std over 5 runs)
PAPER_C2_STD = 0.0246                     # Table 7 (std over 5 runs)
TOL_C1 = 3 * PAPER_C1_STD                 # 0.0189 absolute band
TOL_C2 = 3 * PAPER_C2_STD                 # 0.0738 absolute band


def run_grid(X, y, D, m_grid, seeds, t, agg):
    """One (m, seed) sweep; returns per-run records."""
    recs = []
    for m in m_grid:
        for seed in seeds:
            t0 = time.time()
            s, dg = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed, D=D,
                                return_diag=True, agg=agg)
            dt = time.time() - t0
            ev = evaluate_scores(y, s)          # labels used only after scoring
            recs.append({"m": m, "seed": seed, "t": t, "agg": agg,
                         "auc_roc": ev["auc_roc"], "auc_pr": ev["auc_pr"],
                         "auc_pr_trapz": ev["auc_pr_trapz"],
                         "skipped_fraction": dg["skipped_fraction"],
                         "max_cell_size": dg["max_cell_size"],
                         "wall_seconds": dt})
            print(f"    m={m:4d} seed={seed} AUC-ROC={ev['auc_roc']:.4f} "
                  f"AUC-PR={ev['auc_pr']:.4f} skip={dg['skipped_fraction']:.4f}"
                  f" ({dt:.2f}s)", flush=True)
    return recs


def aggregate(records):
    per_m = {}
    for m in sorted({r["m"] for r in records}):
        rs = [r for r in records if r["m"] == m]
        per_m[m] = {
            "auc_roc": summarize([r["auc_roc"] for r in rs]),
            "auc_pr": summarize([r["auc_pr"] for r in rs]),
            "auc_pr_trapz": summarize([r["auc_pr_trapz"] for r in rs]),
            "skipped_fraction_mean": float(np.mean([r["skipped_fraction"]
                                                    for r in rs])),
            "max_cell_size": int(np.max([r["max_cell_size"] for r in rs])),
            "wall_seconds_mean": float(np.mean([r["wall_seconds"] for r in rs])),
            "auc_roc_per_seed": [round(r["auc_roc"], 6) for r in rs],
            "auc_pr_per_seed": [round(r["auc_pr"], 6) for r in rs],
            "seeds": [r["seed"] for r in rs],
        }
    return per_m


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
                    help="ignore selected_config.json and re-run the grid")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=len(SEEDS_DEFAULT),
                    help="number of repeats (paper: 5)")
    ap.add_argument("--t", type=int, default=T, help="ensemble size (paper: 100)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    seeds = SEEDS_DEFAULT[: args.seeds]
    os.makedirs(RESULTS, exist_ok=True)
    t_start = time.time()

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- data
    print("[1/5] loading ADBench cardio")
    X, y, prov = load_cardio(verbose=True)
    validation = {
        "n_rows": int(X.shape[0]), "n_features": int(X.shape[1]),
        "n_anomalies": int(np.sum(y)), "anomaly_rate": float(np.mean(y)),
        "expected_n": N_EXPECT, "expected_positives": POS_EXPECT,
        "shape_ok": X.shape == (N_EXPECT, 21),
        "positives_ok": int(np.sum(y)) == POS_EXPECT,
        "nan_count": int(np.isnan(X).sum()), "inf_count": int(np.isinf(X).sum()),
        "col_mean_absmax": float(np.abs(X.mean(0)).max()),
        "col_std_min": float(X.std(0).min()), "col_std_max": float(X.std(0).max()),
    }
    # ADBench ships cardio already per-column standardised (assumption A11), so
    # no further rescaling is applied: it cannot change Euclidean orderings.
    validation["already_standardised"] = bool(
        validation["col_mean_absmax"] < 1e-9
        and abs(validation["col_std_min"] - 1.0) < 1e-3)
    validation["signature_ok"] = bool(validation["shape_ok"]
                                      and validation["positives_ok"]
                                      and validation["nan_count"] == 0
                                      and validation["inf_count"] == 0)
    print("      signature:", {k: validation[k] for k in
                               ("n_rows", "n_features", "n_anomalies",
                                "anomaly_rate", "signature_ok",
                                "already_standardised")})
    if not validation["signature_ok"]:
        raise SystemExit(f"cardio signature validation FAILED: {validation}")
